In Rust every value has exactly one owner, and the value is dropped when its owner goes out of scope. Assigning or passing a heap value moves ownership, so the old variable can no longer be used. Borrowing with references lets code read a value without taking it: any number of shared references, or exactly one mutable reference, never both at once. The borrow checker enforces these rules at compile time, which removes use-after-free and data races without a garbage collector. Lifetimes are covered in [[Rust lifetimes]].
